exam_name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which AWS service provides access to multiple foundation models through a single API, allowing developers to experiment with models from Anthropic, Meta, Amazon, and others without managing infrastructure?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker
options.B: Amazon Bedrock
options.C: Amazon Lambda
options.D: Amazon EC2

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that offers access to multiple high-performing foundation models via a single API, including models from Anthropic (Claude), Meta (Llama), Amazon (Titan), and others, without requiring infrastructure management.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: When choosing a foundation model for a summarization task that requires understanding long documents, what is the most important factor to verify?

options.A: The model training dataset size
options.B: The model context window length
options.C: The model inference latency
options.D: The number of model parameters

questions.explanation: The context window determines how much input text the model can process at once. A model with an insufficient context window will truncate long documents, leading to incomplete summaries.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What is the primary difference between pre-training and fine-tuning of a foundation model?

options.A: Pre-training uses labeled data, fine-tuning uses unlabeled data
options.B: Pre-training trains from scratch on broad data, fine-tuning adapts a pre-trained model on task-specific data
options.C: Pre-training is done by AWS, fine-tuning must be done by the user
options.D: Pre-training is free, fine-tuning costs money

questions.explanation: Pre-training trains a model from scratch on a large, general-purpose dataset. Fine-tuning takes an already pre-trained model and further trains it on a smaller, task-specific dataset to improve performance on that specific task.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which prompt engineering technique involves providing the model with a few examples directly in the prompt before asking the actual question?

options.A: Zero-shot prompting
options.B: Few-shot prompting
options.C: Chain-of-thought prompting
options.D: Role prompting

questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting provides the model with a small number of examples (shots) in the prompt to demonstrate the desired task before asking the actual question.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which parameter in the Bedrock InvokeModel API controls the randomness of the models output? Lower values make outputs more deterministic.

options.A: maxTokens
options.B: topP
options.C: temperature
options.D: presencePenalty

questions.explanation: Temperature controls the randomness of output. A lower temperature (e.g., 0.2) makes the model more deterministic and focused, while a higher temperature (e.g., 0.8) makes the output more creative and varied.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: For a code generation task where deterministic, reproducible output is required, what temperature setting should you use?

options.A: Temperature = 1.0
options.B: Temperature = 0.8
options.C: Temperature = 0.5
options.D: Temperature = 0.2

questions.explanation: A low temperature (e.g., 0.2) makes the model deterministic and reproducible by reducing the probability of sampling less likely tokens. For code generation where the same prompt should always produce the same code, a temperature near 0 is ideal.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which prompt structure is most effective for instructing a model to produce output in a specific format?

options.A: Providing the format example at the end of the prompt
options.B: Using XML tags to clearly separate instructions, input, and desired output format
options.C: Embedding the format requirements in a system prompt only
options.D: Asking the model to choose its preferred format

questions.explanation: Using structured delimiters like XML tags helps the model clearly distinguish between instructions, context, and the desired output format, leading to more reliable structured output.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does "stop sequence" mean in the context of foundation model inference?

options.A: The maximum number of tokens the model can generate
options.B: A specific sequence of characters that, when encountered, causes the model to stop generating further tokens
options.C: The sequence in which foundation models are called in a pipeline
options.D: A training technique to make models stop learning

questions.explanation: A stop sequence is a string that, when generated by the model, signals the inference to stop and return the output. For example, setting a stop sequence of "\n\n" would make the model stop at a double newline.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: When comparing foundation models for a chatbot application, you should evaluate each model using which of the following combinations?

options.A: Accuracy on a benchmark dataset only
options.B: Latency, cost per token, and output quality on representative prompts
options.C: Number of model parameters and training data size only
options.D: Inference speed on a single prompt only

questions.explanation: Model selection for production requires balancing latency (response speed), cost per token (prompt + completion pricing), and output quality measured on representative prompts that match your actual use case.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: In a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architecture, what is the purpose of the retriever component?

options.A: To generate the final answer to the user query
options.B: To search and retrieve relevant documents from a knowledge base based on the query
options.C: To embed documents for storage
options.D: To fine-tune the foundation model on custom data

questions.explanation: In RAG, the retriever takes the user query, embeds it into a vector, and searches a vector store to find the most relevant documents. These are then passed to the generator (LLM) to produce a grounded answer.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the role of embeddings in a RAG system?

options.A: To store documents in compressed format
options.B: To convert text into numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning, enabling similarity search
options.C: To encrypt sensitive data before storage
options.D: To compress model weights for faster inference

questions.explanation: Embeddings map text into dense numerical vectors where semantically similar texts are nearby. In RAG, both query and documents are embedded, and similarity search finds relevant documents based on vector proximity.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: When chunking documents for a RAG knowledge base, what chunk size range is typically recommended?

options.A: 10-50 tokens
options.B: 100-400 tokens
options.C: 1000-4000 tokens

questions.explanation: Chunks of 1000-4000 tokens are recommended because they are large enough to contain sufficient context for answering questions but small enough to fit within the models context window alongside the query and retrieved chunks.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which AWS service provides managed vector search capability for RAG systems?

options.A: Amazon OpenSearch Service
options.B: Amazon S3
options.C: Amazon DynamoDB
options.D: Amazon RDS

questions.explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service supports k-NN (k-nearest neighbors) search, enabling vector similarity search for RAG systems. It is the primary managed option for building a vector store on AWS.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of a reranker in a RAG pipeline?

options.A: To re-embed documents using a different model
options.B: To apply a more accurate model to re-rank retrieved chunks by relevance
options.C: To regenerate the query for a second retrieval pass
options.D: To compress retrieved content

questions.explanation: A reranker takes the initial retrieved chunks and applies a cross-encoder model that jointly encodes the query and each chunk to produce precise relevance scores, improving answer quality by filtering out irrelevant results.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: In a RAG system, what problem does groundedness refer to?

options.A: Whether the generated answer is supported by the retrieved documents
options.B: Whether documents are properly stored in cloud storage
options.C: Whether model weights are properly initialized
options.D: Whether the query matches session history

questions.explanation: Groundedness measures whether the LLM response is supported by the retrieved context. A grounded response cites specific information from retrieved documents, while an ungrounded or hallucinated response makes claims not supported by the provided context.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which retrieval method finds the most relevant documents in a vector store?

options.A: Exact string matching
options.B: TF-IDF scoring
options.C: Cosine similarity between query and document embeddings
options.D: Boolean keyword search

questions.explanation: Vector stores use embedding-based similarity search, typically cosine similarity, to find documents whose embeddings are closest to the query embedding. This enables semantic search that captures meaning beyond exact keyword matches.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which scenario is a key advantage of RAG over fine-tuning?

options.A: RAG always produces more accurate results
options.B: RAG does not require retraining and can use up-to-date knowledge without model updates
options.C: RAG is always cheaper
options.D: RAG eliminates prompt engineering

questions.explanation: RAG allows the system to use current information from the knowledge base at query time without retraining the model. New documents can be added to the knowledge base immediately, whereas fine-tuned models need retraining to incorporate new information.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What does context window refer to in a RAG system?

options.A: The maximum number of documents retrievable
options.B: The maximum tokens the model can process including query and documents
options.C: The number of embedding dimensions
options.D: The vector store size in bytes

questions.explanation: The context window is the maximum number of tokens the model can process in a single inference call. In RAG, this accommodates the query, retrieved documents, and generated response.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of metadata filtering in RAG retrieval?

options.A: To filter old documents only
options.B: To narrow search using structured criteria alongside semantic similarity
options.C: To delete irrelevant documents
options.D: To encrypt sensitive data

questions.explanation: Metadata filtering combines semantic similarity search with structured filters on document attributes (e.g., department, date range, document type), narrowing the candidate set and improving precision and efficiency.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: In Amazon Bedrock Agents, what is the role of an action group?

options.A: It defines the security policies for the agent
options.B: It groups together Lambda functions, APIs, and other tools the agent can invoke
options.C: It stores the conversation history
options.D: It configures the foundation model used by the agent

questions.explanation: An action group in Bedrock Agents is a container for tools/functions (Lambda functions, HTTP APIs, etc.) that an agent can call. It also defines the function schema so the agent knows how to invoke them.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which component of a Bedrock Agent maintains conversational state across multiple turns?

options.A: The foundation model
options.B: The action group
options.C: The agent alias
options.D: The knowledge base

questions.explanation: An agent alias represents a deployable version of the agent and can maintain session state. When a user interacts through an alias, conversation context is preserved across turns.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: In an agentic workflow, what distinguishes a reasoning step from an action step?

options.A: Reasoning uses the LLM; action calls external tools
options.B: Reasoning is fast, action is slow
options.C: Reasoning needs internet, action runs locally
options.D: Reasoning happens first

questions.explanation: In the observe-think-act loop, the reasoning step is where the LLM processes observations and decides what to do. The action step executes the decision, typically by calling a tool (Lambda, API, search query).

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: When a Bedrock Agent calls a Lambda function, what information is passed?

options.A: Only the user original query text
options.B: The function name, parameter values from conversation, and session ID
options.C: The full conversation history as JSON
options.D: Only the model output logits

questions.explanation: When a Bedrock Agent invokes a Lambda function, it passes the function name and parameter values extracted from the conversation context, along with the session identifier in the event payload.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the purpose of the prompt flow in a Bedrock Agent?

options.A: To route requests to different models based on cost
options.B: To customize orchestrated prompts that guide agent behavior
options.C: To filter sensitive data from inputs
options.D: To encrypt conversations

questions.explanation: The prompt flow in Bedrock Agents allows customization of orchestrated prompts that guide the agent behavior, including interpreting user intent, deciding whether to call a tool, processing observations, and formatting responses.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which AWS service integrates with Bedrock Agents for long-term agent memory?

options.A: Amazon DynamoDB
options.B: Amazon S3
options.C: Amazon MemoryDB
options.D: Bedrock Agents does not have built-in long-term memory; external storage is required

questions.explanation: Bedrock Agents manages short-term session memory through agent aliases, but for persistent long-term memory across sessions, you must integrate external storage like DynamoDB or a vector database via Lambda functions.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is a cooperative agent pattern?

options.A: An agent that only generates text without calling tools
options.B: An agent that can delegate sub-tasks to other specialized agents
options.C: An agent that only works with open-source models
options.D: An agent that never asks clarifying questions

questions.explanation: In a cooperative multi-agent system, a primary agent can delegate sub-tasks to specialized sub-agents. Each sub-agent handles its domain and results are combined by the orchestrator agent.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which is NOT a valid action type for Bedrock Agent action groups?

options.A: Lambda function invocation
options.B: HTTP API invocation
options.C: Text completion generation
options.D: Knowledge base query

questions.explanation: Bedrock Agent action groups support Lambda invocations, HTTP API calls, and knowledge base queries. Plain text completion is handled by the foundation model directly, not through an action group.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: When should you use a Bedrock Agent versus a simple prompt to a foundation model?

options.A: Agents should always be used; simple prompts are deprecated
options.B: Use an agent for multi-step tasks requiring dynamic reasoning and external tools; use simple prompts for static single-turn tasks
options.C: Use an agent only for Q&A; use prompts for all other tasks
options.D: Agents are cheaper than simple prompts

questions.explanation: Bedrock Agents are for complex, multi-step tasks requiring dynamic reasoning and external tool calls. Simple prompts are sufficient for static tasks like single-turn Q&A without external dependencies.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the maximum number of action groups a single Bedrock Agent can have?
questions.explanation: A Bedrock Agent can have up to 10 action groups (or 15 in some regions). This limits how many distinct tool sets the agent can invoke.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Why should text be cleaned before generating embeddings for a RAG knowledge base?

options.A: To reduce document storage size
options.B: To remove noise like HTML tags and whitespace that can degrade embedding quality
options.C: To convert text to lowercase for faster processing
options.D: To encrypt sensitive information before embedding

questions.explanation: Cleaning and normalizing text (removing HTML tags, extra whitespace, inconsistent formatting) improves embedding quality because embedding models are trained on clean, standardized text. Noisy input degrades embeddings and reduces retrieval accuracy.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the purpose of an embedding model?

options.A: To translate text between languages
options.B: To convert text into numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning
options.C: To generate summary text from documents
options.D: To classify text into predefined categories

questions.explanation: An embedding model maps text into dense numerical vectors where semantically similar texts are nearby in vector space. This enables similarity search and semantic retrieval in RAG systems.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: When chunking documents for embedding, what strategy preserves context across chunk boundaries?

options.A: Making each chunk exactly 500 tokens with no overlap
options.B: Overlapping chunks by a small margin (e.g., 10-20% of chunk size)
options.C: Splitting only at document start and end
options.D: Concatenating all chunks into one large embedding

questions.explanation: Overlapping chunks (sliding window) ensures sentences spanning chunk boundaries are captured in at least one chunk, preventing information loss and reducing retrieval errors for boundary-spanning content.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What does the dimensionality of an embedding vector represent?

options.A: The length of the original text in characters
options.B: A set of learned features capturing aspects of semantic meaning (e.g., 768, 1536, 3072 dimensions)
options.C: The number of words in the original text
options.D: The token count of the original text

questions.explanation: Each dimension in an embedding vector represents a learned latent feature of meaning (not directly interpretable). Common dimensions include 768 (BERT), 1536 (text-embedding-ada-002), or 3072 (text-embedding-3-large). Higher dimensions capture more nuance but increase storage and compute costs.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which distance metric is most commonly used to compare embeddings during similarity search?

options.A: Euclidean distance (L2 norm)
options.B: Manhattan distance (L1 norm)
options.C: Cosine similarity
options.D: Hamming distance

questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors, capturing semantic similarity regardless of magnitude. Two texts with similar meaning but different lengths will have high cosine similarity even if their vector magnitudes differ.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is sparse embedding and how does it differ from dense embedding?

options.A: Sparse embeddings are larger in file size
options.B: Sparse embeddings use term-matching (e.g., TF-IDF) with many zeros; dense embeddings use neural models with mostly non-zero values
options.C: Sparse embeddings are encrypted versions of dense embeddings
options.D: Sparse embeddings are faster to compute but only work with English text

questions.explanation: Sparse embeddings (TF-IDF, BM25) produce vectors with many zero values where each non-zero dimension corresponds to a vocabulary term. Dense embeddings from neural models produce compact vectors where most dimensions are non-zero and represent learned latent features.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the purpose of a vector database in a RAG system?

options.A: To store original text documents in compressed format
options.B: To store and index embedding vectors for fast similarity search at query time
options.C: To host the foundation model for generating responses
options.D: To manage user authentication

questions.explanation: A vector database stores embedding vectors along with metadata and provides efficient indexing (e.g., HNSW, IVF) for nearest-neighbor similarity search at query time. When a query is embedded, the vector DB quickly retrieves the most similar vectors and their associated content.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which technique accelerates similarity search in large vector databases?

options.A: Linear scan of every vector
options.B: Approximate Nearest Neighbor algorithms like HNSW, IVF, or FAISS
options.C: SQL indexing on vector columns
options.D: Hashing the text before embedding

questions.explanation: Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) algorithms like HNSW, IVF, and FAISS enable sub-linear search time in high-dimensional spaces. They trade a small amount of recall for significant speed improvements, crucial for low-latency production RAG systems.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the recommended approach for handling multi-language content in a RAG knowledge base?

options.A: Use a separate embedding model and vector store for each language
options.B: Use a multilingual embedding model that maps all languages into a shared vector space, chunking by language
options.C: Translate all content to English before embedding
options.D: Store only English content and reject non-English queries

questions.explanation: Multilingual embedding models map multiple languages into a shared semantic vector space, enabling cross-lingual retrieval. Chunking should preserve language boundaries so a query in one language retrieves relevant documents in compatible languages.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: In embedding-based retrieval, what does the top-k parameter control?

options.A: The minimum similarity score threshold for retrieved documents
options.B: The number of most similar documents to return for a given query
options.C: The maximum length of the generated response
options.D: The learning rate used when training the embedding model

questions.explanation: The top-k parameter determines how many of the most similar vectors (documents) the retriever returns for a given query embedding. Higher k increases recall but may reduce precision and increase context length; lower k is faster but may miss relevant documents.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Amazon Bedrock guardrail feature?

options.A: To encrypt data at rest
options.B: To filter harmful, biased, or inappropriate content from model inputs and outputs based on configurable policies
options.C: To limit which foundation models can be used
options.D: To authenticate users accessing Bedrock

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails lets you create customizable policies to filter harmful content (violence, hate speech, sexual content, misinformation) in model inputs and outputs, with configurable strength levels.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which IAM permission is required for a user to invoke a foundation model through Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: bedrock:CreateModel
options.B: bedrock:InvokeModel
options.C: bedrock:StartInference
options.D: bedrock:RunModel

questions.explanation: The bedrock:InvokeModel permission is required to invoke a foundation model. It can be scoped to specific model ARNs for least-privilege access control.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is prompt leakage and why is it a security concern in Bedrock Agents?

options.A: The model leaks training data to the user
options.B: The model reveals internal system prompts or instructions to the user, which attackers can use to bypass controls
options.C: The model loses the original prompt during inference
options.D: The prompt is logged without encryption

questions.explanation: Prompt leakage occurs when the model reveals internal system prompts or instructions to users. Attackers can use this information to craft prompt injections that bypass safety controls or extract proprietary configurations.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which AWS service provides managed rate limiting and DDoS protection for Bedrock applications?

options.A: AWS WAF
options.B: AWS Shield
options.C: Amazon CloudFront
options.D: AWS Rate Limiter

questions.explanation: AWS WAF allows you to configure rate-based rules that limit requests from a specific IP or range within a time period, protecting your Bedrock application from abuse or DDoS-style attacks.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: When should sensitive data be redacted before sending to a foundation model?

options.A: Only when the model is fine-tuned
options.B: Always — PII and other sensitive data should be scrubbed from prompts before inference
options.C: Only for text-embedding models
options.D: Never, because models protect user data

questions.explanation: Sensitive data like PII, credentials, and financial info should always be redacted from prompts before sending to a foundation model. The service provider may log this data unless explicitly opted out.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Amazon Bedrock model customization safety feature?

options.A: To encrypt model weights during fine-tuning
options.B: To validate that user-provided training data does not contain toxic or sensitive content before fine-tuning begins
options.C: To limit the number of fine-tuning epochs
options.D: To authenticate the user submitting the fine-tuning job

questions.explanation: Bedrock model customization includes safety validation that checks user-provided training data for toxic, harmful, or sensitive content before fine-tuning begins. This prevents inadvertently fine-tuning a model on data that could cause it to generate harmful outputs.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which Bedrock feature allows you to audit and trace model usage for compliance and security purposes?

options.A: Amazon CloudWatch Logs
options.B: AWS CloudTrail
options.C: AWS Config
options.D: Amazon EventBridge

questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail logs all API calls made to Amazon Bedrock, including InvokeModel and model customization operations. These logs provide an auditable record of who accessed which models and when, supporting security analysis and compliance requirements.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is a prompt map in Bedrock Agents?

options.A: A visual diagram showing how the agent calls tools
options.B: A configuration that defines which foundation model to use for each step of the agent workflow
options.C: A security policy that maps user roles to allowed prompt templates
options.D: A log of all prompts sent to the foundation model

questions.explanation: A prompt map in Bedrock Agents allows you to assign different foundation models to different stages of the agent workflow (e.g., a cheaper model for routine reasoning, a more capable model for complex tasks), optimizing cost-latency-quality trade-offs per step.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which of the following is a best practice for securing API keys used with Bedrock applications?

options.A: Store keys in source code with a .gitignore file
options.B: Store keys in AWS Secrets Manager and reference them via IAM roles at runtime
options.C: Embed keys in environment variables on EC2 instances
options.D: Share keys across all team members via email

questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager provides secure storage, rotation, and access control for API keys and secrets. Applications should retrieve secrets at runtime using IAM role-based access rather than hardcoding keys in source code or environment variables.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Amazon Bedrock Marketplace?

options.A: To buy and sell AWS credits
options.B: To discover, test, and subscribe to third-party foundation models within the Bedrock interface
options.C: To host custom models trained by AWS partners
options.D: To compare Bedrock pricing plans

questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock Marketplace lets customers discover, test, and subscribe to third-party foundation models from AWS partners, all within the Bedrock console. Users can try models with sample prompts before subscribing and then invoke them through the same InvokeModel API.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which AWS service is used to deploy a custom container image containing a foundation model for inference?

options.A: Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS)
options.B: Amazon SageMaker
options.C: AWS Lambda
options.D: Amazon EKS

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker provides managed infrastructure for deploying custom container images containing foundation models for batch or real-time inference, with auto-scaling, load balancing, and A/B testing.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the purpose of provisioned throughput in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: To encrypt model inputs and outputs
options.B: To reserve a fixed number of inference tokens per second for consistent low-latency responses
options.C: To limit the number of model calls per minute
options.D: To cache frequently requested responses

questions.explanation: Provisioned throughput in Bedrock lets you reserve a fixed number of model invocations or tokens per second, ensuring consistent low-latency responses for production workloads.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which CloudWatch metric tracks the number of tokens processed by a Bedrock model invocation?

options.A: InvocationCount
options.B: ModelLatency
options.C: InputTokenCount and OutputTokenCount
options.D: ErrorCount

questions.explanation: CloudWatch emits InputTokenCount and OutputTokenCount metrics for each Bedrock InvokeModel call, enabling cost monitoring and optimization against budget thresholds.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the recommended approach for reducing Bedrock inference costs?

options.A: Use only the smallest model for all tasks
options.B: Implement response caching, use smaller models where possible, and batch requests
options.C: Store model outputs in S3 to avoid re-computation
options.D: Run all models locally

questions.explanation: Cost optimization for Bedrock includes caching responses for repeated queries, selecting appropriately-sized models, and batching multiple inputs when possible. These reduce token consumption while maintaining quality.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which AWS service provides a managed feature store for ML features used in Bedrock fine-tuning jobs?

options.A: Amazon DynamoDB
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store
options.C: Amazon S3
options.D: Amazon Redshift

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store stores, serves, and manages ML features. It provides a centralized repository for features used in Bedrock fine-tuning jobs, ensuring consistency between training and inference.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What does cold start mean in the context of Bedrock model invocation?

options.A: The model weights have not been loaded yet, causing an initial delay before the first response
options.B: The API endpoint is not yet configured
options.C: The model has been idle and needs to be restarted
options.D: The network connection is slow

questions.explanation: Cold start refers to the initial delay when a model endpoint is first invoked or scaled up, as the infrastructure provisions compute instances and loads the model weights into memory. Subsequent invocations are faster as the model stays warm.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which AWS feature helps reduce Bedrock model latency by placing compute closer to users?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront edge locations
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: Multi-region deployment
options.D: Amazon Route 53 latency routing

questions.explanation: AWS Global Accelerator improves global application performance by routing traffic through the AWS global network to the optimal AWS region, reducing latency compared to direct internet access. It provides static anycast IP addresses for improved routing.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which CloudWatch Alarm metric should you monitor to detect when a Bedrock model is consistently returning throttling errors?

options.A: Invocations
options.B: ThrottledRequests
options.C: Error
options.D: ModelLatency

questions.explanation: The ThrottledRequests metric in CloudWatch tracks the number of requests that were throttled due to exceeding account-level or model-level rate limits. Monitoring this helps identify when you need to adjust provisioned throughput or request a quota increase.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the recommended way to handle a model that exceeds your latency SLA?

options.A: Switch to a faster model that still meets accuracy requirements
options.B: Reduce the number of documents retrieved in RAG
options.C: Increase the batch size for more efficient processing
options.D: Move to a different AWS region

questions.explanation: If a model consistently exceeds latency SLAs, switching to a faster model that still meets quality requirements is the most direct solution. Alternatives include optimizing prompt length, reducing context size, or enabling provisioned throughput for the current model.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which AWS service provides real-time observability for Bedrock applications with distributed tracing?

options.A: AWS X-Ray
options.B: Amazon CloudWatch
options.C: AWS CloudTrail
options.D: AWS Config

questions.explanation: AWS X-Ray provides distributed tracing for Bedrock applications, showing the flow of requests through Lambda functions, API Gateway, and other services that call Bedrock. This helps identify latency bottlenecks and debug production issues with end-to-end visibility.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: When using the Bedrock Converse API, what is the benefit of using the system message parameter?

options.A: It replaces the need for prompt engineering
options.B: It sets the behavior and tone of the model for the entire conversation without being part of the conversation history
options.C: It encrypts the conversation
options.D: It limits the model to only respond with pre-approved answers

questions.explanation: The system message parameter in the Converse API sets persistent instructions that guide the model behavior throughout the conversation, such as "You are a helpful coding assistant." These are processed differently from regular conversation turns and influence overall tone and style.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of the parent-child chunking strategy in advanced RAG systems?

options.A: To store child documents in a separate database from parent documents
options.B: To retrieve coarse-grained parent chunks and then fetch their finer-grained child sub-chunks for more precise context
options.C: To encrypt parent and child embeddings separately
options.D: To delete parent chunks after child chunks are created

questions.explanation: Parent-child chunking creates a two-level hierarchy where documents are split into larger parent chunks (coarse) and smaller child chunks (fine-grained). At retrieval time, the system finds relevant parent chunks via similarity search and then fetches all child chunks to provide complete, precise context for the generator.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How does a Bedrock Agent decide whether to invoke a tool or respond directly to the user?

options.A: The agent responds directly; tools are always pre-invoked by the orchestrator
options.B: The foundation model analyzes the user query and decides based on the agent prompt and tool schemas whether a tool call is needed
options.C: Tools are invoked in a fixed sequence regardless of the query
options.D: The agent always invokes the first tool in the list

questions.explanation: The foundation model receives the user query along with tool schemas and decides in its response whether to respond directly or output a structured tool-use request. This decision is part of the agent loop — the model is invoked again after tool results are returned until the query is resolved or a final response is generated.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the difference between passage-level and chunk-level retrieval in RAG?

options.A: Passage-level retrieves whole paragraphs; chunk-level retrieves individual words
options.B: Passage-level retrieves at sentence granularity; chunk-level retrieves at document granularity
options.C: Passage-level retrieval returns the entire source document; chunk-level returns specific text segments
options.D: Both terms are interchangeable

questions.explanation: Passage-level retrieval returns the entire source document (or large passages) that contains the relevant information, while chunk-level retrieval returns specific text segments (chunks) from the document. Chunk-level is more efficient for large documents as it provides only the relevant portion, reducing token usage and improving precision.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the purpose of content filters applied to embedding inputs in Bedrock?

options.A: To compress text before embedding
options.B: To strip or flag potentially harmful content (e.g., PII, hate speech) before creating embeddings
options.C: To increase the embedding vector dimension
options.D: To speed up the embedding process

questions.explanation: Bedrock allows applying content filters (e.g., for PII, hate speech, or other sensitive categories) to embedding inputs before they are processed by the embedding model. This ensures sensitive or harmful data is not encoded into the vector store, maintaining compliance and data safety.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the recommended strategy for testing a Bedrock-powered application before going to production?

options.A: Directly deploy to production and monitor for errors
options.B: Set up a staging environment with realistic traffic simulation and canary deployment
options.C: Test only with the API directly, bypassing your application code
options.D: Use only synthetic data for testing to save costs

questions.explanation: A staging environment with realistic traffic simulation and canary deployment (gradually shifting production traffic to the new version) is the recommended approach. This lets you validate performance, accuracy, and cost under production-like conditions before full rollout.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: When should you use system-level prompting vs. few-shot prompting?

options.A: System-level for tone and behavior, few-shot for demonstrating output format and style
options.B: System-level for output format, few-shot for tone
options.C: Never use both together
options.D: It does not matter; they are interchangeable

questions.explanation: System-level prompting sets the model's role, personality, and behavior (e.g., "You are a terse assistant"). Few-shot prompting provides concrete examples of the desired input-output pattern. Using both together is common — the system message sets the overall behavior while few-shot examples demonstrate the specific format.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of a query expansion or query rewriting step in advanced RAG?

options.A: To encrypt the query for security
options.B: To improve retrieval recall by reformulating the user query into multiple search queries or adding relevant context
options.C: To compress the query for faster processing
options.D: To delete the original query from logs

questions.explanation: Query expansion or rewriting transforms the original user query to improve retrieval. Techniques include generating multiple search queries from one input, adding synonyms, or decomposing complex queries into sub-queries. This increases the likelihood of finding relevant documents that the original query might miss.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How does the maximum turns setting affect a Bedrock Agent conversation?

options.A: It limits the number of documents the agent can retrieve
options.B: It caps how many times the model can invoke tools or generate responses before the conversation must end
options.C: It sets the temperature for model responses
options.D: It limits the context window size

questions.explanation: The maximum turns setting caps the number of conversation turns (model responses + tool calls) the agent can take before the system returns a "maximum depth reached" message. For example, setting max turns to 25 ensures the agent cannot loop indefinitely on a complex task.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the purpose of an embedding cache in production RAG systems?

options.A: To encrypt embeddings at rest
options.B: To store previously computed embeddings and avoid re-computing them, reducing cost and latency
options.C: To convert embeddings back to text
options.D: To compress embedding vectors for faster storage

questions.explanation: An embedding cache stores the embedding vectors for previously processed text (e.g., frequently asked questions or static content). When the same text is encountered again, the cached embedding is returned instead of re-computing, reducing both cost and latency. Cache TTL and eviction policies handle text updates.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the role of a hot start in Bedrock model deployment and how does it differ from a cold start?

options.A: A hot start loads the model into memory for faster subsequent invocations
options.B: A hot start reinitializes the model with pre-warmed weights
options.C: A hot start replaces the need for model serving altogether
options.D: A hot start is a cost-saving measure that delays model loading

questions.explanation: A hot start in Bedrock refers to keeping model instances in a warm state where the model weights are already loaded into memory. This eliminates the initial cold-start latency on subsequent invocations. Provisioned throughput in Bedrock is designed for exactly this purpose — ensuring models stay warm for consistent low-latency production workloads.
